claim: Smad2 is an essential transducer of Nodal signaling during mesendoderm specification in zebrafish.
source: These results demonstrate that Smad2 is an essential transducer of Nodal signaling during mesendoderm specification.
evidence: Demonstrated through MZsmad2 mutant phenotype analysis showing absence of endoderm and mesoderm, rescue experiments with Smad2 expression, and loss of Nodal/Activin activity in MZsmad2 mutants.

claim: MZsmad2 embryos lack endoderm and head and trunk mesoderm.
source: Endoderm and head and trunk mesoderm are absent in MZsmad2 embryos, a phenotype very similar or identical to Nodal loss-of-function mutants (Figure 1C–E) (Feldman et al., 1998; Gritsman et al., 1999).
evidence: Observed phenotype in MZsmad2 mutants shown in Figure 1E and compared to wild-type and MZoep mutants, with citation to previous Nodal mutant studies.

claim: MZsmad2 mutants can be rescued by ubiquitous expression of wild-type Smad2 and GFP-Smad2.
source: MZsmad2 mutants could be rescued by ubiquitous expression of wild-type Smad2 and GFP-Smad2 and the larval lethality of Zsmad2 mutants could be rescued to adulthood by a GFP-Smad2 transgene (Figure 1F–H; Table 1).
evidence: Demonstrated through injection of smad2 and gfp-smad2 mRNA into MZsmad2 embryos and transgenic rescue experiments shown in Figure 1F-H and Table 1.

claim: Neither Nodal nor Activin display any activity in MZsmad2 mutants.
source: Moreover, neither Nodal nor Activin displayed any activity in MZsmad2 mutants (Figure 1I,J).
evidence: Shown by injection of squint (Nodal) and activin mRNA into MZsmad2 embryos with no phenotypic rescue, as depicted in Figure 1I,J.

claim: The long-range target gene ntl is induced at both high and low levels of activated Smad2.
source: Comparing the spatio-temporal maps of Nodal target gene expression and Smad2 activity confirmed that the long-range target gene ntl was induced at both high and low levels of activated Smad2, whereas the expression of the short-range gene gsc correlated with high Smad2 levels and sustained Smad2 activity.
evidence: Determined by comparing spatiotemporal maps of GFP-Smad2 nuclear accumulation with ntl and gsc expression patterns from in situ hybridization.

claim: The expression of the short-range gene gsc correlates with high Smad2 levels and sustained Smad2 activity.
source: Comparing the spatio-temporal maps of Nodal target gene expression and Smad2 activity confirmed that the long-range target gene ntl was induced at both high and low levels of activated Smad2, whereas the expression of the short-range gene gsc correlated with high Smad2 levels and sustained Smad2 activity.
evidence: Determined by comparing spatiotemporal maps of GFP-Smad2 nuclear accumulation with ntl and gsc expression patterns from in situ hybridization.

claim: GFP-Smad2 cells exposed to Nodal for 1 or 2 hours have similar NC ratios.
source: GFP-Smad2 NC ratios were similar in cells exposed to Nodal for either 1 or 2 hr (Figure 3B,E).
evidence: Measured from transplantation experiments where GFP-Smad2 cells were exposed to Nodal for different durations, shown in Figure 3B,E.

claim: The long-range gene ntl is expressed after both 1 and 2 hours of exposure to Nodal.
source: However, while the long-range gene ntl was expressed both after one or 2 hr of exposure to Nodal (Figure 3D,G), the expression of the short-range gene gsc was only detected after 2 hr of exposure (Figure 3C,F).
evidence: Demonstrated through transplantation experiments with RNA in situ hybridization for ntl after 1 and 2 hours of Nodal exposure, shown in Figure 3D,G.

claim: The short-range gene gsc is only expressed after 2 hours of exposure to Nodal.
source: However, while the long-range gene ntl was expressed both after one or 2 hr of exposure to Nodal (Figure 3D,G), the expression of the short-range gene gsc was only detected after 2 hr of exposure (Figure 3C,F).
evidence: Demonstrated through transplantation experiments with RNA in situ hybridization for gsc after 1 and 2 hours of Nodal exposure, shown in Figure 3C,F.

claim: The level of Smad2 activity at a given time does not fully predict target gene expression.
source: These results are inconsistent with the strictest forms of the threshold model—the level of Smad2 activity at a given time predicts target gene expression—and reveal that the duration of signaling influences morphogen interpretation primarily at the level of target gene induction.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that similar Smad2 activity levels at 1 and 2 hours result in different target gene expression patterns (ntl vs gsc).

claim: The duration of signaling influences morphogen interpretation primarily at the level of target gene induction.
source: These results are inconsistent with the strictest forms of the threshold model—the level of Smad2 activity at a given time predicts target gene expression—and reveal that the duration of signaling influences morphogen interpretation primarily at the level of target gene induction.
evidence: Inferred from transplantation experiments showing that duration of Nodal exposure affects target gene expression independently of Smad2 activity levels.

claim: Smad2 activity progressively decreases and reaches basal levels after approximately 60 minutes when cells are moved from high to low Nodal concentration.
source: Inconsistent with the ratchet model, Smad2 activity progressively decreased and reached basal levels after ∼60 min (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Measured by transplanting GFP-Smad2 cells from the margin to the animal pole and tracking NC ratio over time, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The expression of the long-range gene ntl disappears over time after cells are moved from high to low Nodal concentration.
source: Similarly, the expression of the long-range gene ntl disappeared over time (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Demonstrated through transplantation experiments with RNA in situ hybridization for ntl at different time points after transplantation, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Pathway activity and target gene expression cannot be maintained for extended periods after transient exposure to Nodal.
source: Thus, pathway activity and target gene expression cannot be maintained for extended periods after transient exposure to Nodal.
evidence: Inferred from transplantation experiments showing that Smad2 activity and ntl expression decrease when cells are moved from high to low Nodal environments.

claim: Increasing Nodal levels induce higher levels of pSmad2 until a plateau is reached.
source: As predicted by the kinetic model and in agreement with previous studies (Zi et al., 2011), increasing Nodal levels induced higher levels of pSmad2 until a plateau was reached.
evidence: Measured by Western blot analysis of pSmad2 levels after injection of different concentrations of recombinant Nodal protein, with citation to previous studies.

claim: High Nodal levels lead to very rapid activation of Smad2, reaching a quasi-steady state after 1 hour.
source: High Nodal levels lead to a very rapid activation of Smad2, reaching a quasi-steady state after 1 hr.
evidence: Measured by time course Western blot analysis of pSmad2 levels after injection of high concentrations of recombinant Nodal protein.

claim: Low Nodal levels induce lower levels of Smad2 activation and quasi-steady state Smad2 activation is only reached 2 hours after ligand exposure.
source: In contrast, low Nodal levels induced lower levels of Smad2 activation and quasi-steady state Smad2 activation was only reached 2 hr after ligand exposure (Figure 5B).
evidence: Measured by time course Western blot analysis of pSmad2 levels after injection of low concentrations of recombinant Nodal protein, shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Phosphorylation rates for Smad2 activation range from 2.3 × 10−6 to 4.0 × 10−6 nM−1s−1.
source: For Smad2 activation, we found phosphorylation rates (range from 2.3 × 10−6 to 4.0 × 10−6 nM−1s−1) and turnover rates (range from 0.9 × 10−4 to 2.7 × 10−4 s−1) similar to previous studies performed in cell culture and Xenopus animal cap cells (Bourillot et al., 2002; Schmierer and Hill, 2005; Schmierer et al., 2008).
evidence: Determined by fitting the kinetic model to experimental pSmad2 data, with citation to previous studies showing similar values.

claim: Turnover rates for Smad2 activation range from 0.9 × 10−4 to 2.7 × 10−4 s−1.
source: For Smad2 activation, we found phosphorylation rates (range from 2.3 × 10−6 to 4.0 × 10−6 nM−1s−1) and turnover rates (range from 0.9 × 10−4 to 2.7 × 10−4 s−1) similar to previous studies performed in cell culture and Xenopus animal cap cells (Bourillot et al., 2002; Schmierer and Hill, 2005; Schmierer et al., 2008).
evidence: Determined by fitting the kinetic model to experimental pSmad2 data, with citation to previous studies showing similar values.

claim: 47 genes were identified as direct targets of Nodal signaling.
source: This analysis identified 47 direct targets of Nodal signaling.
evidence: Identified using three criteria: increased expression upon Nodal exposure, induction in presence of cycloheximide, and Smad2 binding near transcription start sites.

claim: ntl is induced at low Nodal concentrations and reaches high NanoString counts (~2500) at high Nodal concentrations.
source: For example, ntl, a typical long-range target, was induced at low Nodal concentrations and its expression reached high NanoString counts (∼2500) at high Nodal concentrations.
evidence: Measured by NanoString analysis of ntl expression at different Nodal concentrations.

claim: The induction of ntl expression is rapid, with mRNA accumulating within 30 minutes after injection of intermediate levels of Nodal.
source: The induction of ntl expression was rapid: ntl mRNA accumulated within 30 min after injection of intermediate levels of Nodal and continuously increased over time.
evidence: Measured by NanoString time course analysis of ntl expression after Nodal injection.

claim: gsc requires higher concentrations of Nodal to be detected above background levels compared to ntl.
source: By contrast, gsc, a short-range Nodal target, required higher concentrations of Nodal to be detected above background levels, and its NanoString counts at high Nodal concentrations were 25 times lower than those of ntl.
evidence: Measured by NanoString analysis comparing gsc and ntl expression at different Nodal concentrations.

claim: gsc NanoString counts at high Nodal concentrations are 25 times lower than those of ntl.
source: By contrast, gsc, a short-range Nodal target, required higher concentrations of Nodal to be detected above background levels, and its NanoString counts at high Nodal concentrations were 25 times lower than those of ntl.
evidence: Measured by NanoString analysis comparing gsc and ntl expression at high Nodal concentrations.

claim: The induction of gsc is slow, with mRNA accumulation only detected after 60 minutes.
source: The induction of gsc was slow: mRNA accumulation was only detected after 60 min.
evidence: Measured by NanoString time course analysis of gsc expression after Nodal injection.

claim: Transcription rates for Nodal target genes vary widely, ranging from 0.0016 to 9.3 counts/s with a mean of 0.54 ± 1.66.
source: Reflecting the different transcript levels measured by NanoString, transcription rates varied widely between genes, ranging from 0.0016 to 9.3 counts/s (mean 0.54 ± 1.66).
evidence: Determined by fitting the kinetic model to NanoString data for 47 direct Nodal target genes.

claim: Kds for Nodal target genes range from 0.73 to 42 nM, with more than 75% of Kds between 5 and 10 nM.
source: In contrast, Kds only ranged from 0.73 to 42 nM, with more than 75% of Kds between 5 and 10 nM (Figure 5—source data 7).
evidence: Determined by fitting the kinetic model to NanoString data for 47 direct Nodal target genes.

claim: The Kd of Smad2 for ntl is 4.9 nM.
source: For example, we found Kds of Smad2 for ntl and gsc of 4.9 nM and 5.4 nM, respectively, while the transcription rates were 0.67 counts/s for ntl and 0.032 counts/s for gsc.
evidence: Determined by fitting the kinetic model to NanoString data for ntl.

claim: The Kd of Smad2 for gsc is 5.4 nM.
source: For example, we found Kds of Smad2 for ntl and gsc of 4.9 nM and 5.4 nM, respectively, while the transcription rates were 0.67 counts/s for ntl and 0.032 counts/s for gsc.
evidence: Determined by fitting the kinetic model to NanoString data for gsc.

claim: The transcription rate for ntl is 0.67 counts/s.
source: For example, we found Kds of Smad2 for ntl and gsc of 4.9 nM and 5.4 nM, respectively, while the transcription rates were 0.67 counts/s for ntl and 0.032 counts/s for gsc.
evidence: Determined by fitting the kinetic model to NanoString data for ntl.

claim: The transcription rate for gsc is 0.032 counts/s.
source: For example, we found Kds of Smad2 for ntl and gsc of 4.9 nM and 5.4 nM, respectively, while the transcription rates were 0.67 counts/s for ntl and 0.032 counts/s for gsc.
evidence: Determined by fitting the kinetic model to NanoString data for gsc.

claim: Only very low gsc RNA counts (~50) can be detected 1 hour after Nodal exposure.
source: These differences explain why only prolonged exposure to Nodal induced gsc in the test of threshold model (Figure 3): only very low gsc RNA counts (∼50) can be detected 1 hr after Nodal exposure.
evidence: Inferred from the low transcription rate of gsc and NanoString measurements after 1 hour of Nodal exposure.

claim: ntl is induced at high levels (~1000 counts) after 1 hour of Nodal exposure.
source: In contrast, ntl, which was rapidly induced in the test of the threshold model, was induced at high levels (∼1000 counts) after 1 hr.
evidence: Measured by NanoString analysis of ntl expression 1 hour after Nodal exposure.

claim: The kinetic model recapitulates the spatiotemporal pattern of activated Smad2 observed in vivo.
source: Using these conditions, the spatiotemporal pattern of activated Smad2 correlated well with the endogenous pattern of Smad2 activation (Figure 5B): a short-range low-amplitude gradient was transformed over time into a long-range high-amplitude gradient, as observed in vivo for the GFP-Smad2 activity gradient (Figure 2F,G) (Harvey and Smith, 2009).
evidence: Demonstrated by comparing model simulations with experimental GFP-Smad2 NC ratio measurements over time and space, shown in Figures 2F,G and 5B.

claim: In simulations, ntl expression begins in cells close to the margin 45 minutes after ligand production starts.
source: For example, in our simulations, ntl expression began in cells close to the margin 45 min after ligand production started, and the range of ntl continuously increased and reached cells located more than 100 µm away from the margin after 3 hr (Figures 2H, 6A).
evidence: Generated by running the kinetic model with ntl-specific parameters and comparing to in vivo expression patterns shown in Figures 2H and 6A.

claim: The range of ntl expression reaches cells located more than 100 µm away from the margin after 3 hours.
source: For example, in our simulations, ntl expression began in cells close to the margin 45 min after ligand production started, and the range of ntl continuously increased and reached cells located more than 100 µm away from the margin after 3 hr (Figures 2H, 6A).
evidence: Generated by running the kinetic model with ntl-specific parameters and comparing to in vivo expression patterns shown in Figures 2H and 6A.

claim: gsc expression is delayed and its range of expression is confined to cells close to the source.
source: By contrast, gsc expression was delayed and its range of expression was confined to cells close to the source (Figures 2H, 6B).
evidence: Generated by running the kinetic model with gsc-specific parameters and comparing to in vivo expression patterns shown in Figures 2H and 6B.

claim: foxa3 mRNA rapidly accumulates at high levels up to four cell tiers (~60 µm) from the source and extends up to 80–100 µm by the onset of gastrulation.
source: As predicted by the simulations, foxa3 mRNA rapidly accumulated at high levels up to four cell tiers (∼60 µm) from the source and then extended up to 80–100 µm by the onset of gastrulation (Figure 6C).
evidence: Measured by RNA fluorescent in situ hybridization at different time points and compared to model predictions, shown in Figure 6C.

claim: efnb2a mRNA readily accumulates but is expressed in a narrower domain than foxa3.
source: efnb2a mRNA also readily accumulated but was expressed in a narrower domain, as predicted from the simulations (Figure 6D).
evidence: Measured by RNA fluorescent in situ hybridization at different time points and compared to model predictions, shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Genes that are highly induced by Nodal generally display a long range of expression.
source: In agreement with the simulations, we found that genes that are highly induced by Nodal generally display a long range of expression (Figure 7A,B).
evidence: Demonstrated by comparing maximal expression levels from NanoString data with simulated spatial ranges, shown in Figure 7A,B.

claim: The maximal transcription rate is the best predictor of gene expression range among the kinetic parameters.
source: Strikingly, the maximal transcription rate, not the Kd or the degradation rate, was the best predictor of gene expression range (Figure 7C,D).
evidence: Demonstrated by scatter plot analysis comparing different kinetic parameters with expression range, shown in Figure 7C,D.

claim: The maximal transcription rates for foxa3 and gsc differ by a factor of 20.
source: For example, while the degradation rate, Kd and Hill coefficient for the long-range gene foxa3 and the short-range gene gsc are very similar (Figure 5—source data 7), their maximal transcription rate, and therefore their maximal level of expression, differ by a factor of 20.
evidence: Determined by comparing fitted parameters for foxa3 and gsc from the kinetic model.

claim: A delay in gene induction can reduce the range of target gene expression.
source: Simulations revealed not only the expected delay but also a reduced range of target gene induction: a long-range gene could be transformed into a short-range gene by introducing a delay in gene induction (Figure 8A).
evidence: Demonstrated by extending the kinetic model with a co-factor that delays gene induction and comparing simulations with and without the delay, shown in Figure 8A.

claim: efnb2b is induced slowly after Nodal exposure at 3.5 hpf but more rapidly after exposure at 4.5 hpf.
source: For example, when Nodal was injected at 3.5 hpf, efnb2b was only induced after approximately 2 hr. By contrast, when Nodal was injected at 4.5 hpf, the delay in efnb2b induction was reduced by more than 30 min (Figure 8B).
evidence: Measured by NanoString time course analysis of efnb2b expression after Nodal injection at different developmental stages, shown in Figure 8B.

claim: efnb2b expression is detected only late (6 hpf) and at a short range (5 cell tiers).
source: Strikingly, and as predicted by the delayed induction model, efnb2b expression in the embryo was detected only late (6 hpf) and at a short range (5 cell tiers) (Figure 8C).
evidence: Measured by RNA fluorescent in situ hybridization at different time points, shown in Figure 8C.

claim: bra can only be induced shortly before gastrulation and is expressed at low levels and at a short range.
source: Similarly, the Nodal target gene bra (Martin and Kimelman, 2008) could only be induced shortly before gastrulation and, as predicted by the model, was expressed at low levels and at a short range (Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Measured by RT-qPCR and RNA fluorescent in situ hybridization at different developmental stages, shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2, with citation to previous study identifying bra as a Nodal target.

claim: The kinetics of target gene induction is a major determinant of morphogen interpretation.
source: This approach reveals that the kinetics of target gene induction is a major determinant of morphogen interpretation and suggests that a kinetic model of morphogen interpretation is better suited for the Nodal morphogen system than the prominent threshold and ratchet models.
evidence: Inferred from the combined results of spatiotemporal mapping, transplantation experiments, NanoString analysis, and kinetic modeling.

claim: A target gene can be induced rapidly and at a long range by high transcription rate, high Smad2 affinity and early onset of induction.
source: Thus, a target gene can be induced rapidly and at a long range by high transcription rate, high Smad2 affinity and early onset of induction.
evidence: Inferred from the kinetic model and experimental data showing how different parameters affect gene expression range.

claim: Low affinity for Smad2, low transcription rate or late onset of induction generate short-range gene expression patterns.
source: Conversely, low affinity for Smad2, low transcription rate or late onset of induction generate short-range gene expression patterns.
evidence: Inferred from the kinetic model and experimental data showing how different parameters affect gene expression range.

claim: In a rapidly developing system, the intrinsic rate of transcription of a target gene can be a major determinant of gene expression range.
source: Our results do not contradict such models but reveal that in a rapidly developing system, the intrinsic rate of transcription of a target gene can be a major determinant of gene expression range: high affinity binding sites cannot overcome the limits imposed on gene expression range by low levels of intrinsic transcription.
evidence: Inferred from the finding that transcription rate is the best predictor of expression range and that high affinity alone is insufficient for long-range expression.

claim: High affinity binding sites cannot overcome the limits imposed on gene expression range by low levels of intrinsic transcription.
source: Our results do not contradict such models but reveal that in a rapidly developing system, the intrinsic rate of transcription of a target gene can be a major determinant of gene expression range: high affinity binding sites cannot overcome the limits imposed on gene expression range by low levels of intrinsic transcription.
evidence: Inferred from the comparison of gsc and foxa3, which have similar Kds but very different transcription rates and expression ranges.

claim: Delays in transcriptional onset can turn high affinity target genes into short-range genes.
source: Similarly, delays in transcriptional onset can turn high affinity target genes into short-range genes.
evidence: Demonstrated by simulations and experimental data showing that efnb2b and bra have delayed induction and short-range expression despite having Smad2 binding sites.

claim: The Nodal morphogen gradient forms and extends through diffusion.
source: This approach reveals that the kinetics of target gene induction is a major determinant of morphogen interpretation and suggests that a kinetic model of morphogen interpretation is better suited for the Nodal morphogen system than the prominent threshold and ratchet models.
evidence: Based on the kinetic model which incorporates Nodal diffusion and previous experimental measurements of Nodal diffusion coefficients.

claim: Rapid phosphorylation generates a corresponding gradient of activated Smad2.
source: This approach reveals that the kinetics of target gene induction is a major determinant of morphogen interpretation and suggests that a kinetic model of morphogen interpretation is better suited for the Nodal morphogen system than the prominent threshold and ratchet models.
evidence: Demonstrated by measuring pSmad2 levels at different Nodal concentrations and time points, and by GFP-Smad2 spatiotemporal mapping.

claim: The Nodal signaling pathway plays essential roles in animal development.
source: The Nodal signaling pathway plays essential roles in animal development.
evidence: Established scientific consensus about Nodal signaling function in development.

claim: Nodal signaling induces and patterns mesendoderm and establishes left-right asymmetry.
source: Nodal signaling induces and patterns mesendoderm and establishes left-right asymmetry (Conlon et al., 1994; Shen, 2007; Grande and Patel, 2009; Schier, 2009; Duboc et al., 2010; Shiratori and Hamada, 2014).
evidence: Cited from multiple previous studies on Nodal signaling functions.

claim: The Nodal signaling pathway regulates dozens of genes, ranging from transcription factors to cytoskeletal components.
source: The Nodal signaling pathway regulates dozens of genes, ranging from transcription factors to cytoskeletal components, in order to pattern embryonic tissues (Bennett et al., 2007; Liu et al., 2011; Fodor et al., 2013).
evidence: Cited from previous studies identifying Nodal target genes.

claim: Nodal signaling is required for self-renewal as well as specification of endoderm and mesoderm in embryonic stem cells.
source: In embryonic stem cells, Nodal signaling is required for self-renewal as well as specification of endoderm and mesoderm (James et al., 2005; Vallier et al., 2005; Schier, 2009; Oshimori and Fuchs, 2012; Chen et al., 2013).
evidence: Cited from previous studies on Nodal signaling in embryonic stem cells.

claim: Nodal signals can form concentration gradients and can act as morphogens.
source: Nodal signals can form concentration gradients and can act as morphogens (Chen and Schier, 2001; Williams et al., 2004; Müller et al., 2012, 2013; Xu et al., 2014a).
evidence: Cited from previous studies demonstrating Nodal gradient formation and morphogen activity.

claim: Cells close to the margin activate Nodal signaling earlier and at higher levels than cells at a distance from the margin.
source: Cells close to the margin activate Nodal signaling earlier and at higher levels than cells at a distance from the margin.
evidence: Demonstrated by single-cell tracking of GFP-Smad2 NC ratio over time and space.

claim: During the 1.5 hours from mid- to late-blastula stage, a low-amplitude short-range gradient of activated Smad2 is transformed into a high-amplitude long-range gradient.
source: Thus, during the 1.5 hr from mid- to late-blastula stage a low-amplitude short-range gradient of activated Smad2 is transformed into a high-amplitude long-range gradient.
evidence: Demonstrated by time-lapse imaging and quantification of GFP-Smad2 NC ratio along the vegetal-animal axis.

claim: ntl was first faintly detected in a few cells on the presumptive dorsal side of the embryo at the mid-blastula stage.
source: ntl was first faintly detected in a few cells on the presumptive dorsal side of the embryo at the mid-blastula stage.
evidence: Observed by RNA in situ hybridization time course analysis.

claim: ntl expression domain intensified and progressively extended animally until the onset of gastrulation.
source: Subsequently, its expression domain intensified and progressively extended animally until the onset of gastrulation.
evidence: Observed by RNA in situ hybridization time course analysis.

claim: gsc expression initiated approximately 30 minutes later than ntl and remained confined to a narrow domain on the dorsal side.
source: By contrast, gsc expression initiated ∼30 min later and remained confined to a narrow domain on the dorsal side (Figure 2H).
evidence: Observed by RNA in situ hybridization time course analysis, shown in Figure 2H.

claim: The position of cells relative to the margin does not change extensively until the onset of gastrulation.
source: The resulting spatio-temporal map of Smad2 activity revealed that (1) the position of cells relative to the margin did not change extensively until the onset of gastrulation (Figure 2E)
evidence: Demonstrated by single-cell tracking showing minimal displacement relative to the margin, shown in Figure 2E.

claim: A model in which the maximal transcription rate is gene-specific and Kd is identical for all genes performs better than a model where Kd is gene-specific and the maximal transcription rate is constant.
source: Moreover, multiple hypotheses analysis indicates that a model in which the maximal transcription rate is gene-specific and Kd is identical for all the genes performs better than a model where Kd is gene-specific and the maximal transcription rate is constant (see Nodal signaling modeling section in 'Materials and methods').
evidence: Determined by comparing different model formulations using Bayesian model comparison based on code length.

claim: The gsc probe is less sensitive at low concentrations compared to the ntl probe.
source: The gsc probe is less sensitive at low concentrations.
evidence: Demonstrated by injecting ntl-gsc fusion mRNA at different concentrations and comparing signal intensities from gsc and ntl probes, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The β-actin::GFP-Smad2 transgene rescues smad2/smad2 adult lethality.
source: β-actin::GFP-Smad2 transgene rescues smad2/smad2 adult lethality
evidence: Demonstrated by crossing smad2/+ fish to smad2/+; Tg(GFP-Smad2)/+ fish and recovering adult smad2/smad2 fish only when they carry the GFP-Smad2 transgene, shown in Table 1.

claim: The effective diffusion coefficients and clearance rates of Nodals have been experimentally determined.
source: The effective diffusion coefficients and clearance rates of Nodals have been experimentally determined (Müller et al., 2012), but other parameters of the system have not been measured.
evidence: Cited from previous study that measured Nodal diffusion and clearance parameters.

claim: The range of expression is affected most dramatically by changes in transcription rate, Kd or Hill coefficient.
source: Exploring the contribution of each of these parameters in regulating target gene expression revealed that multiple parameter combinations could simulate the expression patterns observed in vivo (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1). In particular, the range of expression is affected most dramatically by changes in transcription rate, Kd or Hill coefficient.
evidence: Demonstrated by systematic parameter exploration using the kinetic model, shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The degradation rate influences the range of expression only when mRNA half-lives are very short.
source: In the simulations described above (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1), genes whose Kd is low and maximal transcription rate is high are expressed at high levels and at long range. In contrast, the degradation rate influences the range of expression only when mRNA half-lives are very short (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Demonstrated by systematic parameter exploration using the kinetic model, shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Genes with delayed induction contain Smad2/FoxH1 binding sites and show a clear response upon injection of Nodal.
source: Similar to the canonical target genes, genes with delayed induction contained Smad2/FoxH1 binding sites and showed a clear response upon injection of Nodal (Figure 8—figure supplement 1) but their induction was abolished in the presence of cycloheximide (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP-seq analysis showing Smad2/FoxH1 binding and NanoString analysis showing Nodal-dependent induction, shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: The induction of genes with delayed response is abolished in the presence of cycloheximide.
source: Similar to the canonical target genes, genes with delayed induction contained Smad2/FoxH1 binding sites and showed a clear response upon injection of Nodal (Figure 8—figure supplement 1) but their induction was abolished in the presence of cycloheximide (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Demonstrated by NanoString analysis of gene expression after Nodal injection in the presence of cycloheximide, shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Genes with delayed induction are likely to be regulated not only by Nodal signaling but additional factors.
source: These Nodal target genes are therefore likely to be regulated not only by Nodal signaling but additional factors.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that these genes have Smad2/FoxH1 binding sites but their induction is abolished by cycloheximide, suggesting requirement for additional protein synthesis.

claim: Transcriptional delay might be achieved by a co-activator for target gene induction.
source: Transcriptional delay might be achieved by a co-activator for target gene induction.
evidence: Proposed mechanism based on the observation that delayed genes require protein synthesis (cycloheximide sensitivity) and show stage-dependent induction kinetics.

claim: A repressor might have to be eliminated for a target gene to become competent to respond.
source: Alternatively, a repressor might have to be eliminated for a target gene to become competent to respond.
evidence: Proposed alternative mechanism to explain delayed gene induction.

claim: Transcription rates might be influenced by local chromatin structure, promoter strength, and by co-activators that boost or repressors that dampen the levels of target gene expression.
source: Transcription rates might be influenced by local chromatin structure, promoter strength, and by co-activators that boost or repressors that dampen the levels of target gene expression (Li et al., 2007; Lupien et al., 2008; Hager et al., 2009; Kanodia et al., 2012; Peterson et al., 2012; Coulon et al., 2013; Oosterveen et al., 2013; Foo et al., 2014; Xu et al., 2014b).
evidence: Proposed mechanisms based on citations to previous studies on transcriptional regulation.

claim: The intensity and onset of target gene transcription can be major determinants in shaping morphogen gradient interpretation.
source: In either case, our study suggests that the intensity and onset of target gene transcription can be major determinants in shaping morphogen gradient interpretation.
evidence: Inferred from the combined experimental and modeling results showing that transcription rate and induction timing strongly affect expression range.
